new_roles.title: Sr. Director, Club Operations - Boston
new_roles.description:
**Sr. Director, Club Operations - Boston**

Overview

**WHO WE ARE**

Equinox is a category of one, setting the global standard for luxury health, wellness, and hospitality. Our spaces are intentionally elevated, our standards uncompromising, and our expectations high. We attract people who take pride in excellence, care deeply about quality, and want to be part of something that feels different the moment you walk through the door.

We are builders, operators, and innovators who believe great environments and meaningful human connection change lives. Diversity, belonging, and ownership aren’t slogans here, they’re how we work. At Equinox, colleagues don’t just support the business; they shape the future of wellness. Because for us, it’s not fitness. It’s life.

**WHAT WE DO**

We create premium, immersive experiences where performance, hospitality, design, and human connection converge-and every detail matters. This is not a traditional fitness environment. It is a place where high standards, accountability, and pride in craft define the work.

Fueled by an entrepreneurial mindset, we trust our people with real responsibility and real impact. Growth is earned through action, learning is hands‑on, and careers are built by those who want to operate at the highest level. At Equinox, we don’t just offer opportunities-we offer long‑term pathways for people who want to do meaningful work in an environment that expects more and delivers more.

Job Description 
Reporting to the Regional Vice President of Operations, the Sr. Club Operations Director will be responsible for maintaining Equinox Standards across an assigned market area. This leadership role demands a deep understanding of Club management, with a focus on driving sales, enhancing the member experience, and ensuring that the Equinox’s luxury image is consistently upheld. The Sr. Director of Club Operations will lead and manage a group of General Managers and will with closely to lead Club and Ancillary teams, implement strategic initiatives and hold teams accountable for delivering results. The Sr. Director of Club Operations will have a strong presence in driving membership sales, maintaining operational excellence, and fostering a culture of success, guided by our core values.

**Operations Management**

* Member experience and satisfaction
* Facilities maintenance and cleanliness
* Staff management and development
* Group fitness programming
* Personal training programs
* Compliance with safety and hygiene standards

**Financial Performance**

* Achieve revenue targets and control expenses
* Manage budgets and analyze financial reports
* Identify opportunities for growth and profitability

**Team Leadership**

* Recruit, hire, train, and develop department managers
* Foster a positive and collaborative work environment
* Motivate and inspire staff to achieve goals
* Conduct performance reviews and provide feedback

**Member Engagement**

* Build relationships with members and address their needs
* Resolve member complaints and issues
* Create a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere
* Brand Standards:
* Ensure adherence to Equinox brand guidelines and service standards
* Maintain a high level of professionalism and presentation

\*

* Implement marketing and promotional initiatives

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Daily**

* Team Engagement - huddles, meetings, workouts
* Coaching GMs - Focusing on leadership and strategy
* Club Visit and Walk Through - 1-2 clubs/day
* 1on1 business meetings with GMs, AGMs and Regional Leaders

* Review clubs appointments - previous day activities (prospects, sales, equifits)
* Structured 1on1 GM Meetings - 30 min in person at least 2-3x/week
* Schedule Accountability - Checking schedules on arcon, verifying in person

**Monthly**

* GM & AGM development - ensuring it's happening (either directly or GM is delivering), schedule, reviews, learning

* People Pipeline - Staffing for future needs, identifying talent for growth
* Sales Strategy and Accountability - ensure systems and processes are being followed
* Alignment and collaboration with regionals - AE, Ancillary, Sales
* Attend PT Forums when applicable
* Stepping in when the GM requires support
* Full facility inspections - 2/week
* Meet with Regional leaders ancillary every other week/monthly
* Calls - RVP Regional call, Senior Club Director call, GM call

**PERFORMANCE TARGETS:**

100-110% in the following areas:

* New Sales
* Attrition
* Total Operating Revenue/Earnings
* Total Contribution/Profit

Qualifications

* 10+ years of experience in club operations, hospitality, fitness, or a related industry, with at least 3 years in a Sr. leadership role
* Proven track record of overseeing multiple clubs (units) or a high-volume club (facility)
* Strong background in upholding operational efficiency, utilizing & implementing standard operation procedures (SOPs), and ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory standards
* Experience in facility management, including maintenance, equipment, vendor relations, and tech integrations for operational excellence
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, P&L management, and cost control
* Ability to develop and implement revenue growth strategies through membership sales, service offerings, and ancillary revenue streams
* High proficiency in financial reporting, KPI tracking, and data-driven decision-making
* Demonstrated ability to lead, inspire, and develop high-performing teams across multiple functions of the business
* Experience in talent acquisition, performance management, and employee engagement
* Strong leadership presence with the ability to drive a positive culture of accountability and performance
* Understanding of member engagement strategies, retention, and delivering an exceptional member experience
* Strong commitment to member engagement scores and ability to utilize feedback and implement improvements
* Strong problem-solver and decision maker
* Internal Employees:No RODs in the last 6 months

**Pay Transparency: $150,000-160,000 annually: eligible for additional bonus opportunities**

**This role is based in the Boston market and requires regular travel within the assigned micro-market to support business needs and operational priorities.**

Additional Information 
**AS A MEMBER OF THE EQUINOX TEAM YOU WILL RECEIVE:**

* We offer competitive salary, benefits, and industry leading commission opportunities for club employees
* Complimentary Club membership
* Perks and incentives with our products and services including Personal Training, Pilates, Spa and Shop

This job description is intended to describe the general requirements for the position. It is not a complete statement of duties, responsibilities, or requirements. Other duties not listed here may be assigned as necessary to ensure the proper operations of the department.

**Equinox is an equal opportunity employer. For more information regarding our career opportunities, please visit one of our clubs or our website at** ***https://careers.equinox.com/***

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. Must have a legal right to work in the United States.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

Lead manufacturing operations across Karman's El Monte and Corona locations, aligning machining, fabrication, and downstream processing with business objectives. In this role, you will drive safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability by providing operational leadership, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and advancing continuous improvement initiatives across complex manufacturing environments.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads and coordinates manufacturing operations across the El Monte and Corona locations, establishing accountability, performance expectations, and operating rhythms for operations managers and functional departments.
* Develops and executes operational plans that align production performance, capacity, and investment priorities with company strategy.
* Oversees machining, fabrication, forming, finishing, and assembly operations to improve throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, and profitability.
* Drives operational excellence by implementing procedures and standards that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and regulatory compliance.
* Champions Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement through 5S, Kaizen, flow and lead-time improvements, cycle-time and setup reduction, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and preventative maintenance.
* Analyzes financial and production data, including overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), spindle utilization, and labor efficiency, to manage budgets, inventory, spending, and cost performance.
* Ensures equipment readiness, maintenance execution, and manufacturing capacity align with production requirements.
* Partners with human resources on workforce planning, recruiting, organizational structure, labor utilization, work scheduling, leadership development, performance evaluation, and succession planning.
* Coordinates closed-loop communication and escalation across operations, engineering, quality, supply chain, and program management.
* Manages the administration and performance of subcontracted and temporary labor services.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience that includes a minimum of 10 years of relevant manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including oversight of complex production environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration (MBA), Master of Science (MS), or another advanced degree.
* Operational leadership experience in precision manufacturing supporting aerospace or defense production.
* Leadership experience in a computer numerical control (CNC) machining environment producing large, tight-tolerance metallic components.
* Experience machining aluminum using 3-axis and 5-axis milling and large gantry equipment.
* Experience with automated or semi-automated manufacturing equipment.
* Experience managing multi-step manufacturing routings and complex production flows.
* Working knowledge of deburring, finishing, forming, welding coordination, heat treatment, and assembly operations.
* Experience building high-performance manufacturing teams and leading Lean transformation.

**Physical Requirements**

* Frequently sits, uses a computer, and communicates.
* Occasionally stands, walks, reaches, or stoops.
* Uses close vision and works with screens for extended periods.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

**Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Company‑paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short‑ and long‑term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Director-Quality Management - Acute | Highland Hospital | Charleston, West Virginia

**About the Job:**

PURPOSE STATEMENT:  
  
The Director of Quality, Risk & Compliance leads and coordinates quality and performance improvement, regulatory compliance, and patient safety efforts within the healthcare facility. This role ensures that all programs operate within local, state, federal, and accreditation standards, while driving a culture of continuous improvement, clinical excellence, and risk reduction.

**Roles and Responsibilities:**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Provides oversight of all facility programs, including inpatient and outpatient services, ensuring alignment with quality, risk management, patient safety, and regulatory standards.
* Leads facility-wide quality, risk, and patient safety strategy and improvement efforts.
* Directs the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, including development, implementation, and evaluation; monitors KPIs and ensures governance of data-driven improvement efforts.
* Drives organization-wide performance improvement initiatives through data analysis and system-level process enhancements to improve outcomes.
* Oversees incident reporting, investigations, and risk analyses (RCA/Event Analysis), ensuring timely resolution and prevention of recurrence.
* Maintains compliance with all local, state, federal (CMS), and accreditation standards (TJC), ensures ongoing survey readiness, and serves as the primary liaison during regulatory and accreditation surveys, audits, and required reporting activities.
* Partners with the Legal, Compliance, and Risk Department on high-risk events, complaints/allegations, investigations, and corrective action planning.
* Supports the development, review, and implementation of facility policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and consistent adherence across departments.
* Collaborates with department leaders and Human Resources to support staff accountability and ensure adherence to facility policies and procedures.
* Provides staff training and mentoring to support competency, accountability, and adherence to quality, risk, and safety standards, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and patient safety.
* Conducts leadership rounding, medical record reviews, and monitoring of environment of care, safety, and documentation standards.
* Prepares and maintains required reports and documentation; participates in committees, meetings, audits, and organizational initiatives.
* Supervises Patient Advocate/Coordinator roles, when applicable, through hiring, orienting, performance assessment and management, motivating, training, scheduling, and coaching to meet department and facility goals. Supports resolution of patient concerns and patient rights processes.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of patient safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of client safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.
* May serve as Privacy/Security Officer, providing direction and oversight of activities related to compliance with applicable Federal and State law and regulations governing the privacy and security of health information.
* May serve as Chief Healthcare Disparities Officer, leading efforts to identify, analyze, and reduce disparities in care for the populations served.
* May be required to provide onsite coverage for other programs when needed, develops, and executes new programs according to market needs and may provide training, case consultation and Administrator On Call coverage during and after program hours as needed.

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s degree with a clinical, nursing or business emphasis required. Master’s degree in Human Services preferred.
* Three years’ experience in quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, risk management, survey management, behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, or related experience required.
* Knowledge and understanding of state/federal regulations, Joint Commission and/or CARF Accreditation.

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* CPHQ Preferred
* Professional clinical license issued by the appropriate licensing body as required by the state.
* CPR and de-escalation and restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility

**WORK LOCATION:**

This position is onsite at the facility and is not a remote position.

**SUPERVISORY REQUIREMENTS:**

Two years’ supervisory/management experience in behavioral health preferred.

Why Highland Hospital?Highland Hospital offers a comprehensive benefit plan and a competitive salary commensurate with experience and qualifications. Qualified candidates should apply by submitting a resume. Highland Hospital is an EOE.

Veterans and military spouses are highly encouraged to apply. Summit BHC is dedicated to serving Veterans with specialized programming at our treatment centers across the country. We recognize and value the unique strengths of the military community in supporting our mission to serve those who have served.

existing_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.**  
  
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

  

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

  

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) environment.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable. Direct leadership of quality teams is preferred.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

  

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

  

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected.  
  
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is looking for an experienced Senior Director of Quality to join our battery manufacturing organization. In this role you will lead the Quality department for Form Energy. Your scope will be company-wide and your team will implement systems and processes that ensure products are designed, manufactured and shipped to the highest levels of performance, reliability, and quality.

This role is for an executive leader with experience developing new technologies and bringing high-volume manufacturing facilities to life. You will provide vision, strategy and leadership to help Form achieve manufacturing scale, cost-reduction, and daily operation execution.

As the key driver for shipping the highest quality products, you will thrive when working closely with leadership and cross-functional teams throughout the product development lifecycle, from early R&D to validation testing, pilot builds, and ultimately commercial production of customer-facing products.

*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Develop and sustain a world-class quality management system powered by a highly-trained, flexible, and proactive staff
* Maintain product risk profiles and manage quality systems to ensure Form Energy is meeting or exceeding risk expectations
* Ensure Form Energy production operations are releasing only conforming products to our customers
* Communicate key risks and opportunities to leadership and provide direction to resolve top issues and drive definitive corrective action
* Plan and efficiently manage Quality resources (labor, OpEx, and CapEx) and report on department performance and needs
* Communicate Form Energy's commitment to quality with internal and external interested parties
* Drive a customer-focused culture anchored by strong individual ownership and accountability

### **What you'll bring:**

* At least 10 years experience in quality, manufacturing, or manufacturing engineering
* At least 5 years in a senior-leader / site-leader quality role, demonstrating a clear record of success in building industry-leading teams that can execute in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
* Expertise in building Quality Management Systems (e.g., IATF 16949, ISO9001).
* Highly technical background, with a strong foundation in logical reasoning that allows for a steep learning curve and the ability to adapt to new technologies
* Excellent leadership, project management, communication, and organizational skills
* Bachelor’s Degree (or higher) in Engineering

### **Where you'll work:**

This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. **Relocation assistance is available.**

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*  
  
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

Provides strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, ensuring that quality systems, processes, and practices support business objectives, customer requirements, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence. Establishes quality strategy, policies, objectives, and performance expectations and provides leadership across functions to drive continuous improvement, strengthen quality performance, mitigate risk, and support business growth.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

With locations in Indiana, Michigan, Texas, Ohio, and Arizona, we are expanding access to our unique model of care across the United States. Join NPH and become part of a team that is daring to do things differently and making a lasting difference in the lives of our patients, families, and communities every day.

Overview:

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals is looking for a Director of Quality and Risk at our **Huber Heights, OH** location. You will be joining a team of rock star staff who provide exceptional, patient-centered care and understand our patients are always our number one priority! The Director of Quality supports the implementation and monitoring of the quality assurance measurements and audits, and assists in improving patient safety processes throughout the hospital through coordinating and engaging in activities to proactively promote implementation of evidence based best practices and resolve deficiencies; plans, develops, and directs system activities and protocols across NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals; helps to prepare NPH facilities for surveys by accrediting and licensing agencies; serves as a resource to all departments and personnel.

Responsibilities:

Are you a quality leader who enjoys building systems, developing teams, and creating a culture of continuous improvement? Advantic Building Group is seeking a Director of Quality to lead enterprise-wide quality strategy, establish a scalable Quality Management System (QMS), drive ISO 9001 certification efforts, and partner with leaders across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and field operations to deliver exceptional customer outcomes. This is a unique opportunity to build and shape the future of quality within a growing organization.

At Advantic Building Group, we design, fabricate, and install innovative Fiber Reinforced Polymer (FRP) structural systems that help our customers build smarter, safer, and more efficiently.

But what truly sets Advantic apart isn’t just what we build — it’s **how** we work and **who** we work with.

We're a team that values ownership, camaraderie, and curiosity. We roll up our sleeves, tackle challenges together, and support one another along the way. As we continue to grow, we're looking for a quality leader who shares those values and can help strengthen the culture we've built while establishing the systems, processes, and accountability necessary to deliver exceptional quality outcomes for our customers.

**Why Join Advantic?**

* Lead the development of a scalable enterprise-wide Quality Management System (QMS)
* Drive Advantic's ISO 9001 certification journey
* Influence quality across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and field operations
* Build and develop a growing quality organization
* Partner directly with senior leadership to shape strategic initiatives
* Make a visible impact on customer success, operational excellence, and company growth

  

**Role Summary**

The Director of Quality provides strategic leadership for quality across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, assembly, and field operations. This role is responsible for developing and executing Advantic Building Group's quality strategy, building a scalable Quality Management System (QMS), leading ISO 9001 certification efforts, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This leader partners closely with operations, engineering, supply chain, and project teams to reduce defects, improve process performance, strengthen customer confidence, and support the company's growth objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Quality Leadership and Strategic Planning**

* Develop and execute a quality roadmap aligned with business growth, customer commitments, operational risks, and manufacturing and construction requirements; set annual objectives, priorities, and resource needs, including staffing, inspection equipment, and quality technology.
* Report quality performance, emerging risks, and cost of poor quality (scrap, rework, field repairs, returns, warranty) to senior leadership with clear owners, deadlines, and escalation expectations, and partner with Operations and Delivery to reduce it.

**Quality Management Systems (QMS) & ISO 9001 Leadership**

* Develop, implement, and continuously improve Advantic's Quality Management System (QMS), while leading ISO 9001 certification readiness, certification audits, surveillance audits, and recertification activities.
* Build a scalable, practical Quality Management System that enables operational consistency, supports growth, improves customer satisfaction, and achieves ISO 9001 certification.
* Govern document, configuration, and revision control across engineering drawings, submittals, production information, and field documentation, and ensure quality records are reliable and accessible across ERP, MES, and document systems with defined data ownership.

**Manufacturing Quality, Process Control & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish inspection and test plans, acceptance criteria, and release controls for incoming materials, in-process fabrication, final assembly, packaging, and pre-shipment verification, ensuring products conform to approved drawings, engineering requirements, customer specifications, and applicable contractual and industry requirements.
* Partner with Operations on specification review, design reviews, process risk assessments, first-build validation, and readiness for new or changed products and processes; coordinate qualified technical resources when specialized expertise is needed.
* Define traceability, inspection records, measuring equipment controls, calibration, and measurement method validation appropriate to risk and application.
* Establish controls for FRP materials and structural assemblies, including storage, handling, fabrication, and special processes.

**Corrective Actions, Root Cause Analysis & Quality Improvement**

* Lead the enterprise nonconformance and corrective action process, including containment, material disposition, root cause analysis, escalation management, and verification of corrective action effectiveness across internal, supplier, customer, and field-related issues.
* Exercise authority under approved procedures to quarantine material, hold shipments, or stop affected work when conformity is in question; coordinate technical dispositions and obtain required customer approval for concessions or deviations, while maintaining independence of quality decisions.

**Supplier, Subcontractor, & Field Quality Management**

* Partner with Supply Chain to establish supplier qualification, approval, audit, and performance monitoring, including quality requirements for outsourced services and subcontracted work, and maintain approval status in the approved supplier system.
* Ensure certifications, traceability, inspection evidence, and customer requirements are flowed down to suppliers and verified.
* Lead supplier corrective actions and improvement plans, and support cost recovery within established commercial authority.
* Develop the field quality program for construction management and data center white space work, including project quality plan templates, inspection and test plan requirements, hold and witness points, and documentation standards that on-site QC managers must follow.
* Set expectations for, train, and hold on-site QC managers accountable to the program through project kickoffs, periodic field audits, and review of inspection records, field non-conformances, and punch list and turnover documentation.
* Serve as the escalation point for field quality issues and the senior quality contact for customers and third-party inspectors during audits and handover.

  

**Performance Measures**

* Establish baselines, targets, and reporting definitions with leadership. Measures include first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, nonconformance recurrence and closure time, corrective action effectiveness, supplier performance, customer complaints, field deficiencies, audit completion, calibration compliance, and progress against the quality roadmap.

  

**People Leadership and Shared Accountability**

* Lead hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and development of quality personnel, with training matrices, competency expectations, and succession plans.
* Partner with operational leaders to build quality awareness across the organization, and hold process owners accountable through agreed governance and escalation, reinforcing that each department owns the quality of its work.
* Model Ownership, Camaraderie, and Curiosity through clear expectations, respectful challenge, and consistent follow-through.

  

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, quality, or a related discipline, or equivalent directly relevant experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including five or more years leading a quality team or function in manufacturing or a comparable technical environment.
* Demonstrated success building, implementing, or significantly improving Quality Management Systems (QMS).
* Experience leading ISO 9001 implementation, certification readiness, and managing internal, customer, and third-party audits.
* Proven results developing people, leading change across departments, and reducing defects, repeat failures, or quality-related costs.
* Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and inspection requirements; practical knowledge of measurement systems, traceability, process controls, and structured problem-solving.
* Experience using ERP, MES, electronic quality systems, or comparable tools to establish dependable workflows and actionable reporting.
* Ability to communicate clearly with customers, frontline employees, and senior leaders; make sound decisions under pressure; and resolve competing quality, schedule, and business priorities.

  

*Preferred Qualifications*

* Experience with FRP or composite products, structural fabrication, engineered assemblies, construction quality, or mission-critical and data center projects.
* Experience connecting manufacturing quality with field installation, subcontractor oversight, customer acceptance, and project turnover.
* ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, or CQA certification; ISO 9001 lead auditor qualification; or Lean Six Sigma training with demonstrated application.

  

**Physical demands**

While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to communicate effectively through speaking and listening. The role typically involves prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The employee may occasionally be required to stand, walk, reach with hands and arms, and lift or move objects up to 15 pounds.

*Advantic Building Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.*

**DEFINITION:**

Under general direction from the General Manager, plans, directs, organizes, integrates and provides oversight of ReGen Monterey’s Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), equipment maintenance, site and facilities maintenance, landfill operations; scales operations, landfill gas operations, and Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) operations; directs and manages the development of short and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the Strategic Plan and annual business plan and ensures their effective execution; ensures all assigned operations and functions serve the needs of ReGen Monterey, while complying with applicable laws and regulations; responsible for maximizing the environmental management of resources; provides highly responsible and complex operations support to the General Manager.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:**

This position is responsible for coordination, integration and short and long-range planning of a wide variety of functions related to solid waste processing, recycling and diversion programs for ReGen Monterey. Incumbents work at an advanced professional level on complex and specialized solid waste-related operations, recycling activities, facilities, programs, and services, which include formulation and implementation of programs and financial budgets. Within assigned areas of accountability, the incumbent operates with substantial latitude and discretion to achieve effective and efficient utilization of resources in serving ReGen Monterey’s mission. Positions at this class level serve as a member of ReGen’s leadership team and provide advice and counsel to the General Manager regarding strategic policy and problem-solving issues relating to the assigned Departments and ReGen’s overall. A person appointed to the Director of Operations classification is an “at-will” employee.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

*The following duties are typical of this classification and are intended only to describe the various types of work that may be performed, the level of technical complexity of the assignment(s) and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties. The omission of a specific duty statement does not exclude it from the position if the work is consistent with the concept of the classification or is similar or closely related to another duty statement to address business needs and changing business practices.*

* Oversee and is responsible for planning and execution of all aspects of solid waste and recycling operations including processing, recycling/diversion, scheduling, expansion and renovation of processing facility, and customer service.
* Oversee logistics, material preparation and export compliance of collected materials and manage all aspects of commodity sales and related contracted services.
* Oversees and is responsible for the planning and execution of all aspects of the operation and maintenance of ReGen Monterey’s landfill; oversees proper compliance with specifications on the use and development of disposal site, ensures proper operations compliance with health and safety regulations.
* Participates in the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities of ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Plans, organizes, controls, integrates and evaluates the work of assigned departments to ensure services comply with the policies and strategic direction set by the General Manager, Board of Directors and all applicable laws and regulations.
* Recommend and enforce State waste reduction/recycling regulations and other policy issues, including safety policy and procedures.
* Manages the development, revision, and implementation of policies and procedures for ReGen Monterey’s solid waste and recycling/diversion operations.
* Drafts budget for assigned departments.
* Reviews and assesses all program production data; measures program effectiveness; prepares quarterly and annual data reports.
* Assists in the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for equipment and services; represents the division in negotiations with vendors and service contractors and participates in contract administration in disputed contractual matters.
* Prepares staff reports and letters, including reports for presentation to Board of Directors.
* All ReGen Monterey positions require the employee to provide good customer service to both internal and external customers, maintain positive and effective working relationships with other ReGen Monterey employees, and have regular and reliable attendance and timeliness. Must show cooperation and respect to fellow employees and supervisors at all times.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBLITIES:**

The incumbent in this position provides direct supervision of the operations department managers and has oversight of multiple departments and indirect supervision of approximately 100 assigned department employees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Through subordinates, supervises the safe and efficient handling and disposal of solid waste, including household, industrial, infectious, medical, and household hazardous materials; provides oversight ancillary solid waste operations, including equipment maintenance and repair, recycling, and enforcement of refuse disposal laws.
* Coordinates solid waste processing operations with engineering staff to ensure the success of new programs and facilities; analyzes field operations and formulates improvements to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations; performs long-range planning for staffing needs, equipment replacement, and other operational requirements.
* Provides oversight to HHW program and organics recycling program, including food waste collection, yard waste processing, mulch/compost marketing and other waste reduction processing such as scrap metal, electronic waste, mattresses, and scrap tires.

* Prepares tonnage reports and makes recommendations regarding change in fees.
* Organize and optimize the structure of the assigned departments, adjusting in accordance with workloads and new/changing functions.
* Maintain contact with various governmental and regulatory agencies, industry related agencies, and represent ReGen Monterey at public and professional organizations functions.
* Selects and trains operations staff; assists management staff in resolving the most difficult operational problems; establishes productive standards and measures staff performance; accordingly, prepares annual performance plans, evaluates performance, and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinate managers. Collaborates with human resources with disciplinary actions.
* Directly or through subordinates, responds to complaints from ReGen Monterey customers by explaining and enforcing applicable laws and regulations; participates in public workshops to explain and generate support for proposed projects and facilities; may address the Board of Directors to answer questions about issues or proposals related to ReGen Monterey’s operations.
* Oversees and participates in the annual review and revision of ReGen Monterey’s fee structure; develops strategies and approaches for evaluating fee change alternatives; directs the development and recommends proposed fees; attends and participates in public meetings; oversees the implementation of new fees following board approval.
* Directs and coordinates the preparation of analyses and recommendations regarding policy issues and long-range plans to address ReGen Monterey’s financial needs; advises the General Manager regarding policy issues, programs and projects to meet ReGen Monterey and customer needs; advises and assists the General Manager in identifying, articulating and implementing policies, programs and projects.
* Participates in the analysis of proposed legislation and regulation; participates in industry and intergovernmental activities to influence legislative and regulatory change consistent with ReGen Monterey’s interests and needs; represents ReGen Monterey as requested or assigned in dealings with stakeholders in ReGen Monterey’s service area, and with other industry and governmental agencies and professional organizations.
* Participates in major negotiations with contractors, consultants, vendors, collective bargaining and other public agencies.
* Participates in regional, state, national and other professional meetings and conferences to stay abreast of trends and technology related to ReGen Monterey’s operations, particularly in areas of assigned accountability.

**Knowledge of and Ability to:**

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to successfully perform the assigned duties.

**Knowledge of:**

Principles and practices of recycling and diversion program operations, solid waste management and landfill maintenance practices and procedures; local, state and federal regulations pertaining to environmental management of landfills and public works systems or landfill operations; California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); principles and practices of budgeting, effective management, supervision, evaluation and training; health and safety regulations. Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint) is required.

**Ability to:**

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; understand highly regulatory issues (current and proposed) and appropriate permitting for solid waste facilities, recycling operations and programs; negotiate with the best interest of ReGen Monterey; work independently with minimal supervision; manage and evaluate the work of others; prepare clear and concise plans, specifications, and technical reports; interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations; present proposals and recommendations clearly, logically and persuasively in public meetings; develop and implement appropriate procedures and controls; exercise sound, independent judgment within policy guidelines; develop and administer departmental goals, objectives, and procedures; analyze and assess programs, policies, and operational needs and make appropriate adjustments; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods and techniques; facilitate group participation and consensus building; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

**TRAINING, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental planning and management; environmental studies; solid waste planning or a related field is required.

**Experience:**

* Ten to 15 years of broad and progressively responsible work experience in recycling program operations, transfer station management, or combined and related experiences.
* A minimum of five years of recent experience in solid waste management and/or in the operation of mixed waste processing facility or a single-stream material recovery facility or operation of a landfill is required. **OR** work experience in a management position with a private or public agency responsible for solid waste management, recycling/diversion or landfill operations to demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities to meet the above minimum requirements.

**License or Certificate:**

* Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required.

**PhYSICAL AND SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:**

**Physical Demands**

While performing the duties of this class, employees are regularly required to sit; talk or hear, in person, in meetings and by telephone; use hands to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; and reach with hands and arms; occasionally bend, stoop, lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 pounds individually. Employees are occasionally required to walk and stand on even and uneven surfaces, grounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Mental Demands**

existing_roles.description:
**Director, New Product Introduction (NPI) & Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)**

Round Rock, Texas | Onsite | Full-Time

**Reports to:** CFO/CEO

**Works closely with:** Director of Operations/Engineering/R&D, Quality, Purchasing, Production, Program Management and external suppliers

**Travel:** Approximately 25%-35%, primarily to supplier locations

**Role structure:** Hands-on director role; initially an individual contributor leading cross-functional work

**Role Summary**

The Director of NPI & PLM leads the transition of new and modified products from development into stable production. The role coordinates product documentation, supplier readiness, pilot builds, production handoff and lifecycle changes across Ametrine and its manufacturing partners.

This position is focused on practical execution. The Director will work directly with cut-and-sew partners and other suppliers to ensure products can be produced repeatedly at the required quality, capacity and schedule. The role also helps develop alternate sources and contingency plans across fabric, metallization, printing, DWR treatment and cut-and-sew operations.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**New Product Introduction**

* Maintain the NPI schedule for new products, product changes and manufacturing transfers.
* Coordinate requirements, design release, sourcing, prototype builds, pilot production, validation and production handoff.
* Use clear stage gates, owners, due dates and readiness checklists.
* Identify schedule, supplier, material, quality and capacity risks early and drive actions to closure.
* Provide concise status updates covering progress, open decisions, risks and next steps.

**Prototype-to-Production Transfer**

* Work with Engineering and R&D to review designs for manufacturability and production readiness.
* Prepare or coordinate BOMs, routings, work instructions, technical packages, inspection points and packaging requirements.
* Lead prototype, pilot and first-production builds at Ametrine and supplier locations.
* Capture lessons learned and ensure changes are reflected in released documentation.
* Confirm that Operations and suppliers are ready before a product is released to routine production.

**Cut-and-Sew and Supplier Readiness**

* Work onsite with cut-and-sew partners to establish and improve production methods.
* Review patterns, sewing specifications, fixtures, templates, work instructions and inspection requirements.
* Assess supplier labor, equipment, training, floor space, quality controls and available capacity.
* Develop practical ramp plans and verify production rates through actual builds.
* Support supplier training and resolve manufacturability, throughput and quality issues during launch.
* Track supplier actions and escalate missed commitments or unsupported plans.

**Product Lifecycle Management**

* Maintain control of released BOMs, specifications, approved materials, suppliers, routings and product revisions.
* Coordinate engineering changes and assess their impact on inventory, suppliers, schedule, testing and customer requirements.
* Ensure the correct product configuration is used for each order and customer.
* Support PLM process and system improvements, including appropriate integration with ERP/MRP.
* Maintain orderly lifecycle records from product introduction through sustainment and retirement.

**Supply-Chain Resilience**

* Maintain a process-level supply-chain map covering fabric, metallization, printing, DWR, cut and sew, accessories and final delivery.
* Identify bottlenecks, long-lead items, single-source dependencies and supplier-capacity risks.
* Develop and qualify alternate sources where practical.
* Create contingency plans for specialized processes that cannot be economically dual-sourced.
* Coordinate source qualification with Operations, Purchasing, Engineering and Quality.
  

**Quality and Process Control**

* Partner with Quality to define process controls, inspection requirements and first-article expectations.
* Support supplier qualification, process reviews, root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Monitor first-pass yield, defects, rework and launch-related issues.
* Ensure production methods remain consistent with approved documentation and customer requirements.

**Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Lead NPI work through influence across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Purchasing and suppliers.
* Maintain clear owners, deadlines and escalation paths.
* Coordinate with the Director of Operations so new-product timelines and supplier readiness are aligned with the production plan.
* Support communication and coordination between Ametrine Inc. and Ametrine Ltd. where product development activities overlap.

**Success Measures**

* NPI milestones completed on schedule
* Prototype-to-pilot and pilot-to-production cycle time
* Supplier readiness and capacity verification completed before launch
* Percentage of critical supply-chain nodes with an alternate source or documented contingency
* Launch first-pass yield, rework and defect performance
* Completeness and accuracy of BOMs, routings, work instructions and product revisions
* Timely closure of supplier, manufacturing-readiness and lifecycle risks

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, industrial technology, textiles, supply chain or a related field; equivalent directly relevant experience may be considered.
* Eight or more years of relevant experience in NPI, manufacturing engineering, supplier development, PLM, product transfer or contract manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience moving physical products from prototype through pilot and into production.
* Experience working directly with external manufacturers or suppliers.
* Working knowledge of BOMs, routings, work instructions, engineering changes and configuration control.
* Experience with ERP/MRP and PLM or related product-data systems.
* Strong project planning, follow-through, problem-solving and written communication skills.
* Ability to work onsite in Round Rock and travel approximately 25%-35%.
* U.S. citizenship required due to the defense-related nature of the company’s work.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with technical textiles, sewn products, outdoor equipment, military products, automotive soft goods, medical textiles, inflatables or related manufacturing.
* Experience with cut-and-sew production methods, patterns, line balancing or labor standards.
* Experience with coated, laminated, printed or metallized fabrics.
* Defense, aerospace or government-contract manufacturing experience.
* Experience qualifying secondary suppliers or developing business-continuity plans.
* PMP, Lean Six Sigma, APICS or similar certification.

**Working Style**

* Hands-on and comfortable working at supplier facilities and on production floors
* Organized, practical and attentive to manufacturing details
* Able to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, supplier managers and company leadership
* Persistent in following actions through completion
* Comfortable balancing several product introductions and production issues at the same time
* Focused on building useful processes without unnecessary bureaucracy

For more than 140 years, Prysmian has helped shape the infrastructure that powers progress. From helping illuminate the Statue of Liberty in 1886 and delivering power from Hoover Dam to Los Angeles in 1935, to supporting New York City's rebuilding efforts after September 11, our cables and connectivity solutions have played a role in some of history's most significant milestones.

**What You’ll Bring:**

**Experience and Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, business administration, or related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Build bench strength and succession plans for critical operations roles across all sites; partner with HR on talent acquisition, development, and retention strategies.
* Foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement; conduct regular site visits and gemba walks.
* Standardize best practices across facilities and lead cross-site knowledge sharing to eliminate performance variability between plants.
* Champion an EHS-first culture; ensure all locations meet or exceed OSHA and applicable regulatory requirements, with measurable reduction in incident rates.
* Ensure consistent adherence to quality management systems (e.g., ISO 9001) and customer quality requirements across all sites.
* Oversee compliance with environmental, labor, and applicable trade/export regulations at each facility.
* Lead deployment of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and/or Continuous Improvement methodologies across all locations.
* Drive standardization of processes, work instructions, and systems (ERP/MES) to improve consistency, data integrity, and decision-making across sites.
* Identify and lead major process improvement, automation, and cost-savings projects with measurable ROI.
* Partner with Supply Chain/Planning to align production schedules with demand, inventory targets, and on-time delivery goals.
* Collaborate with Engineering on new product introductions, process qualifications, and manufacturability improvements.

=======================

Micro-Tronics, Inc. is a precision aerospace manufacturing company committed to operational excellence, quality, and continuous improvement. We are seeking a results-driven Director of Operations to lead our manufacturing operations and drive performance across production, quality, supply chain, maintenance, and workforce planning. This role is instrumental in delivering customer commitments, achieving revenue objectives, improving operational efficiency, and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**Position Summary**
====================

The Director of Operations oversees daily plant operations with primary accountability for reducing past-due orders, improving manufacturing efficiency, and achieving company revenue targets while maintaining the highest standards of quality and safety. This position provides strategic and operational leadership across manufacturing operations, labor planning, production scheduling, budgeting, and continuous improvement initiatives. The Director of Operations aligns production capacity, scheduling, and shipments with customer commitments and business objectives while driving corrective actions when performance falls short.

**Key Interactions and Relationships**
======================================

Internal: Senior Management, Assembly, Machining, Elastomer Manufacturing, Quality Control, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Human Resources.

External: Customers, Suppliers, Regulatory Agencies and Governing Bodies.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* Supervise and manage plant personnel, including recruiting, training, coaching, and performance management.
* Plan, organize, direct, and manage daily operations to reduce past-due orders, improve manufacturing efficiency, and achieve revenue objectives.
* Develop and improve manufacturing processes to increase throughput and labor productivity while reducing cycle times, downtime, scrap, and rework.
* Oversee production scheduling, maintenance, and logistics to ensure customer delivery commitments are achieved.
* Monitor past-due orders, prioritize recovery efforts, and eliminate material and capacity constraints.
* Manage operational budgets and expenses.
* Ensure all products meet customer requirements, regulatory standards, and company quality objectives.
* Maintain a safe work environment through enforcement of company policies, procedures, and OSHA requirements.
* Manage operational budgets and expenses while aligning production and shipment performance with monthly and quarterly revenue goals.
* Establish and maintain effective controls over capital expenditures, operating expenses, staffing, and labor costs.
* Maintain and review operational scorecards and KPIs while coordinating corrective actions with Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and Human Resources.
* Drive resolution of safety incidents, customer returns, nonconformances, production scrap, inventory concerns, and supplier performance issues.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**
=====================================

* Operational efficiency and productivity

* Mentorship and team-building skills.

* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong organizational and time management skills.

This is an active position requiring the ability to:

* Stand and walk for extended periods.

* Lift and move up to **50 pounds**.
* Work throughout manufacturing environments, including elevated work areas and outdoor conditions when necessary.
