Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description:**

Shield AI is actively seeking candidates with deep expertise in manufacturing and quality methodologies, paired with a relentless drive to enable supplier success and strengthen mission-critical operations.

Shield AI’s Supply Chain Quality team is responsible for global quality oversight across our supplier base. The team reduces supply-chain risk through supplier assessments and internal risk reviews, proactively drives supplier qualification and development activities.

In this role, you will lead a supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, development, performance management, and quality assurance across Shield AI’s aerospace and defense supply base. You will set supplier-quality priorities; manage team capacity, technical execution, and resource allocation; and develop high-performing quality leaders. The role also oversees supplier audits, nonconformance resolution, root-cause investigations, and hands on hardware dispositions.

You will evaluate supplier capability, quality performance, organizational risk, and resource needs to ensure purchased hardware and materials meet Shield AI engineering, customer, regulatory, and quality requirements. As an experienced aerospace quality leader, you will partner closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Program teams to resolve complex supplier-quality issues, improve supplier capability, and reduce quality and delivery risk across the supply base.

**What you'll do:**

* Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
* Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
* Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
* Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
* Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
* Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.
* Advance supplier-quality processes, business systems, data analytics, and continuous-improvement practices that strengthen supplier capability, product quality, delivery performance, and supply-base resilience.

**Required qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or another related technical discipline.
* At least 7 years of relevant experience, including 2–5 years of leadership or people-management experience with direct responsibility for Quality Engineering and/or Supplier Quality Engineering personnel.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and/or ISO 9001 quality-management systems, as well as aerospace and defense supplier-quality requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methods, including 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis.
* Experience with supplier qualification, supplier development, PPAP, and First Article Inspection processes, including AS9102 requirements.
* Understanding of ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and other requirements applicable to aerospace and defense suppliers.
* Demonstrated people-leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, organizational development, and building high-performing technical teams.
* Strong cross-functional collaboration, executive communication, and supplier relationship-management skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.
* Experience using ERP/MRP systems.
* Ability to travel to Shield AI manufacturing locations and supplier sites domestically and, as needed, internationally—up to approximately 20% of the time.

**Preferred qualifications:**

* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent quality certification.
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Experience leading supplier-quality functions in a high-growth aerospace, defense, autonomy, robotics, or advanced-manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting the production and qualification of complex electromechanical, electronic, precision-machined, composite, or avionics hardware.

existing_roles.title: Director, Industrial Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE TEAM**
------------------

Anduril's Manufacturing Engineering Team is seeking a Director, Industrial Engineering to lead IE strategy and execution for the Air Defense & Strike (AD&S) division. The Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware — including static equipment, moving ground equipment, sensors, undersea, and flight vehicles — and scaling these products across our production footprint, including our new 5M sq ft manufacturing facility, Arsenal-1.

Industrial Engineering at Anduril operates in a matrix with a Center of Excellence (COE) and embedded IEs directly into the divisions they support. Every embedded IE takes day-to-day direction and priorities from their business line, while the central IE organization provides the methodology, standards, tools, mentorship, career development, surge coverage, and cross-divisional visibility that make each individual IE more effective than they could be on their own. The Director, IE — AD&S is the senior IE leader dedicated to one of Anduril's highest-growth, most operationally complex divisions — owning the IE strategy, team, and results for AD&S and operating as a peer member of the division's production leadership team.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**
------------------

As the Director, Industrial Engineering — AD&S, you will own the industrial engineering function for the Air Defense & Strike division end-to-end. You will build, lead, and develop the IE team embedded in AD&S — hiring the right people, designing the team structure, and setting the IE agenda in lockstep with the division's production strategy and ramp trajectory and COE standards and enterprise vision / system. You report to the Director of Industrial Engineering (central IE CoE) and sit as a peer alongside AD&S production leadership, connected to the VP of Production, Director of Manufacturing Engineering, and Program Directors who shape division priorities.

This is a division-level leadership role with enterprise accountability. You are not inheriting a mature, steady-state operation — AD&S is in active ramp across multiple product lines, standing up new production systems, scaling from prototype through low-rate into full-rate production, and doing so at a pace that demands IE leadership who can build the plane while flying it. You will define what IE looks like for AD&S: which capabilities to stand up first, how to staff and structure the team, where to invest in labor standards, layouts, simulation, and capacity planning, and how IE integrates into the division's NPI and production ramp cadence.

You will translate company-wide IE standards and the Manufacturing Development Plan (MDP) into AD&S-specific execution — adapting central methodology to the division's unique product mix, production maturity, and operational tempo while maintaining consistency with enterprise IE standards and Core 4 reporting. You are accountable for IE outcomes across the division: labor standards coverage, layout quality, line balance efficiency, capacity model accuracy, and the measurable impact of IE on AD&S production performance.

The right person for this role is a seasoned IE or manufacturing engineering leader who thrives in start-up and ramp environments — someone who has built teams from scratch, stood up production systems, and driven measurable operational impact in fast-moving, complex manufacturing. You have deep technical credibility in IE fundamentals but lead through strategy and people: setting vision, building organizational capability, and creating the systems that let a growing team deliver at scale. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, making decisions with incomplete information, and operating at the intersection of divisional execution and enterprise IE strategy. You communicate with clarity and conviction to senior leadership and are energized by the challenge of building something new in a high-stakes environment.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

**Divisional IE Strategy and Execution**

* Own the IE strategy for AD&S — defining the roadmap, capability priorities, and investment plan aligned to the division's ramp trajectory, NPI pipeline, and business objectives.
* Translate company-wide IE standards and the MDP process into AD&S-specific execution — ensuring IE deliverables (labor standards, layouts, line balances, capacity models) are completed at the right maturity gates and integrated into division planning.
* Drive Core 4 metrics performance (labor hours per unit, line balance efficiency, throughput, units per square foot) — setting targets, tracking results, and ensuring IE work moves the numbers that matter to AD&S. IE provides the roadmap to scale.
* Serve as the primary IE interface to AD&S leadership for capacity questions, ramp feasibility, layout approvals, make-vs-buy analysis, and production system design. Connect AD&S needs to central IE capabilities and enterprise resources.

**Team Building and Leadership**

* Build the AD&S IE team into a high-performing, right-sized organization — designing the structure, defining roles, leading hiring, and onboarding IEs, IE Leads, and IE Technicians aligned to the division's product lines and production stages.
* Directly manage the embedded IE team — setting expectations, driving accountability, conducting performance reviews, and investing in the growth and career development of every team member. Own the headcount plan and budget.
* Develop high-potential talent, build succession depth, and ensure every IE is proficient in core methodology (time studies, MODAPTS/MTM, line balancing, layout design, capacity modeling, Core 4 measurement).

**Production System Design and NPI**

* Lead IE involvement in production line stand-ups and NPI ramps — from process characterization and layout design through labor standards development, line balancing, rate-readiness validation, and system optimization.
* Own production line and workstation layout design — cell configurations, material flow, equipment placement, and spatial planning for both low-rate and full-rate production using simulation-backed approaches.
* Drive capacity planning and production modeling — ensuring AD&S has accurate capacity models, proactively identifying bottlenecks and constraints, and supporting capital investment decisions with IE analysis.

**Cross-Functional Partnership and Communication**

* Operate as a peer member of the AD&S production leadership team — shaping production strategy, influencing capital and staffing decisions, and representing IE in all forums where production decisions are made.
* Build strong working relationships across Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Program Management, and Facilities. Represent AD&S IE in cross-divisional forums, bringing enterprise best practices back to the division.
* Be present on the floor. Walk the lines, build credibility with operators and supervisors, and model the Gemba-first, data-driven culture the IE team stands for. Communicate IE impact to senior leadership with clarity and conviction.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
* 12+ years of experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, or production operations, with demonstrated depth across multiple IE disciplines (labor standards, layout design, capacity planning, simulation).
* 5+ years managing industrial engineers or manufacturing engineers, including experience managing managers or leads — with demonstrated hiring, org design, and team-building experience.
* Experience building or scaling an IE team in a ramp or start-up production environment — designing team structure, hiring into it, and standing up capabilities from early stages.
* Deep technical credibility in core IE fundamentals: time studies, labor standards (MTM/MODAPTS), line balancing, layout design, capacity planning, and production system design.
* Experience operating as a peer of production leadership — influencing strategy, owning budgets and headcount, and communicating IE impact to VP-level audiences.
* Track record of driving measurable operational improvement — IE initiatives that moved production metrics and can be quantified.
* Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, MBA, or a related field.
* Experience in defense, aerospace, or other highly regulated, high-mix manufacturing environments with complex compliance and traceability requirements.
* Experience standing up a centralized or embedded IE function from scratch — methodology selection, standards development, tooling, and organizational adoption.
* Proficiency in simulation software (FlexSim, Arena, AnyLogic, or equivalent), data analytics/visualization (Power BI, Tableau), or experience integrating IE deliverables with MES/ERP platforms.
* Experience designing and commissioning new production lines or manufacturing facilities.
* Active security clearance, or ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

  

### **Benefits**

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

  

### **Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* **Please always verify communications:**

  + Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
* **Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:** If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

### **Data Privacy**

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

This leader directs a team of fulfillment operations planners, order management specialists, and execution coordinators, steering initiatives in order backlog reduction, multi-site distribution throughput, order consolidation, and peak seasonal readiness. Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it's a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn't been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

**Overview**

Scout Motors is seeking an Employee Operations Leader to build and lead the infrastructure that powers exceptional employee experiences at scale. This leader will own Scout's HR service delivery, systems ecosystem, and data governance — the operational backbone of the HR function.

As Scout grows, this role will be responsible for ensuring that every employee has seamless access to HR support, that our HR technology is configured and governed to support accurate data and reliable operations, and that our processes are disciplined, efficient, and continuously improving. This leader will partner closely with the Chief Human Resources Officer, HR centers of excellence, IT, Finance, and business leaders to build a high-performing HR operations function fit for a fast-scaling company.

#### **What you'll do**

Leadership & Team Development

* Lead, develop, and coach a team spanning HR operations, HR systems architecture, and LMS administration.
* Set a clear vision for HR operations and inspire the team to deliver consistent, high-quality service to employees and people leaders.
* Create a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence within the team.
* Partner with the CHRO and HR leadership team to align operational priorities with the broader HR strategy.
* Champion inclusion, collaboration, and Scout's cultural values within the team and across the function.

HR Service Delivery & Operations

* Lead continuous improvement of service delivery processes to improve the employee and people leader experience, with heavy focus on ensuring HR data quality and enabling self service capabilities.

HR Systems & Technology

* Own Scout's HR technology ecosystem, including HRIS, LMS, ATS, and potential future talent marketplace platforms.
* Partner with IT, vendors, and HR centers of excellence to evaluate, implement, and optimize HR technologies.

* Where necessary, establish a workflow for inquiries that require greater consideration and action from HR Partners or other Subject Matter Experts.

* Ensure integrations between HR systems are stable, accurate, and aligned with business needs.
* Stay current on HR technology trends and proactively identify opportunities to modernize or streamline the HR tech stack.

Data, Reporting & Governance

* Own Scout's HR data strategy, reporting infrastructure, and workforce analytics capabilities.
* Establish data governance frameworks, standards, and audit processes that ensure data quality, accuracy, and compliance.
* Partner with Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders to deliver workforce reporting and insights that inform people and organizational decisions.
* Build dashboards and reporting tools that give leaders visibility into the health and performance of the workforce.

**Location & Travel Expectations**:

* This role requires 4 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
* **Travel**: Domestic and minimal international travel may be required as business needs evolve. Valid driver's license required. Passport required

#### **What you'll bring**

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You'll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You'll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

* Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree, MBA, or advanced HR-related degree preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive HR experience with significant experience in HR operations, HRIS, or shared services leadership.

* Demonstrated grit, curiosity, and resourcefulness in navigating ambiguity, solving complex problems, and turning obstacles into practical, scalable solutions.

#### **What you'll gain**

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. As a Director of Operational Excellence here at Honeywell, you will be responsible for leading and overseeing the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across multiple business units.

As a Director of Operational Excellence here at Honeywell, you will be responsible for leading and overseeing the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across multiple business units. You will play a critical role in driving operational excellence and continuous improvement. As a strategic leader, you will collaborate with senior leaders to identify improvement opportunities and develop a strategic roadmap for HOS aligned with business goals. If you are a visionary leader with a passion for driving change and operational excellence, this is the perfect opportunity for you. Join us at Honeywell and be part of a talented team dedicated to shaping the future.

  

YOU MUST HAVE

* 8+ years of experience and mastery in implementing and driving continuous improvement initiatives
* Strong knowledge of Lean Six Sigma methodologies
* Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment
* Ability to clearly and concisely communicate at all levels of the organization.
Ability to travel up to 50%  

WE VALUE

* Strategic mindset and ability to align HOS initiatives with business objectives
* Ability to lead and inspire cross-functional teams
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Passion for continuous improvement and driving change  

The annual base salary range for this position is $189,000 - $235,000. This position is incentive plan eligible. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information visit: Benefits at Honeywell

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

  

Key Responsibilities

* Strategize and oversee the success of the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across the business
* Work with the individual sites to Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for HMX, aligning it with business goals and objectives
* Provide guidance and mentorship to HMX Senior Managers and teams in implementing Lean methodologies and tools
* Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of HMX site assessments initiatives, making recommendations for enhancements
* Prepare monthly updates with sites and Senior management aligned with deliverables for each of the sites under scope of responsibilities.
* Participate in operational improvements as needed within the sites under scope of responsibilities to include productivity improvements tied to continuous improvement.

  
Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy.

existing_roles.title: Director of Operations Excellence
existing_roles.description:
**Brand:**

Bagel Brands

**Bagel Brands is the parent company for your favorite breakfast brands, Einstein Bros. Bagels, Bruegger's Bagels, Noah's NY Bagels, and Manhattan Bagel. We believe in the bagel and how it has the unique ability to bring people together. Our team has a standard set of values and behaviors that allow us to spread a little more joy and happiness in the world. They let us laugh, smile, and enjoy each other’s company a little more. These are the behaviors that guide how we work, how we treat each other, and how we treat our guests. We believe that there is no better way to make someone’s day than with a warm, fresh-baked bagel and a heart-felt good morning.**

**POSITION MISSION**

The Director, Operations Excellence leads the strategy, team, and discipline that make it easier for our bakery teams to obsess over our guests and deliver great results every day. This role owns the enterprise operations engineering agenda for Bagel Brands — evaluating how work gets done, designing better ways of working, and building the team needed to test, scale, and sustain change across Field Operations and Support Center teams.

  

In alignment with Bagel Brands’ Mission, Vision, and Values, this role builds an organization that helps teams Take Ownership of better ways of working, Support Each Other through thoughtful change, and ultimately creates simpler, more consistent operations that allow bakery teams to Obsess Over Our Guests.

  
  

Department: Operations

Salary: $180,000 to $200,000

Annual Bonus: 20%

Long Term Incentive Plan: $30,000

  

**RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:**

**Strategic Leadership & Vision**

* Set the multi-year vision and roadmap for Operations Excellence, aligning priorities with enterprise strategy and Field Operations needs.

* Build and prioritize a portfolio of process engineering and continuous improvement initiatives across the bakery system.

* Represent Operations Excellence in senior leadership and strategic planning forums, translating field findings into enterprise decisions.

  
  

**Operations Excellence & Process Engineering**

* Oversee evaluation of bakery processes, workflows, and systems to simplify work, optimize labor investments, reduce waste, and strengthen performance.

* Guide application of Lean, Six Sigma, process mapping, and root-cause analysis across a portfolio of concurrent initiatives.

* Own the standard for future-state process design, balancing efficiency, guest experience, team member experience, and financial impact.

* Ensure the team produces process maps, standard work, and tools that translate solutions into repeatable bakery practices at scale.

  
  

**Testing, Piloting & Continuous Improvement**

* Set the standard for how the organization designs and governs operational pilots before broader rollout.

* Review pilot results with senior leadership and make scale, refine, or discontinue recommendations.

* Sponsor root-cause analysis on significant recurring challenges, ensuring solutions are sustainable rather than short-term fixes.

  
  

**Labor and Inventory Analytics and Systems Optimization**

* Own labor and inventory system optimization through consistent review of program enhancements, labor/inventory performance opportunities, and cross-functional partnerships with IT, Finance, and program owners.

* Create and maintain regular reporting for Ops teams that highlights opportunities for improvement

  
  

**Project & Change Management**

* Own the portfolio of cross-functional operational excellence initiatives from problem identification through sustainment.

* Set the organization’s approach to structured change management and ensure it is applied consistently.

* Maintain enterprise-level visibility to portfolio progress, risks, and business impact.

  
  

**Team & Field Leadership**

* Build, lead, and develop a team of Operations Excellence managers and professionals.

* Coach the team on problem solving, project management, and change leadership, building bench strength for future roles.

* Maintain regular presence in bakeries, partnering with Field Operations leaders to test and validate solutions.

* Identify successful practices within the bakery system and lead efforts to standardize and scale them.

  
  

**Cross-Functional Partnership & Measurement**

* Partner with Training, Technology, Marketing, Culinary/R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, and Development to evaluate the impact of enterprise initiatives.

* Represent the Operations perspective in cross-functional and executive-level project governance.

* Own the measurement framework used to demonstrate whether operational improvements are delivering results.

* Deliver clear, data-driven recommendations and portfolio updates to senior Operations leadership.

  

**LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES (DIRECTOR / SENIOR DIRECTOR)**

* *Effective Communication:* Articulates vision and manages difficult conversations cross-functionally; communicates complex initiatives and navigates executive discussions.
* *Accountability & Ownership:* Owns budget and strategy and drives a culture of accountability; manages multi-team performance and champions data-driven decisions.
* *Adaptability & Perseverance:* Leads the department through major change and anticipates trends; drives change across functions and builds resilient teams.
* *Empowerment:* Creates space for innovation and mentors emerging leaders; designs structures for decentralized decision-making.
* *Curiosity:* Probes beyond surface issues and fosters a learning environment; benchmarks against top organizations and sponsors new ideas.
* *Self-Awareness:* Understands own leadership brand and exhibits humility; holds deep clarity on values and stays resilient under pressure.

  

**REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Required**

* 10+ years of experience in restaurant operations, operations excellence, continuous improvement, or a related discipline.

* 3+ years of experience directly leading and developing a team.

* Track record of leading enterprise-scale, cross-functional projects with measurable business impact.

* Strong strategic, analytical, and structured problem-solving skills.

* Strong portfolio and project management skills, with the ability to manage senior stakeholders and budgets.

* Demonstrated ability to influence and drive change at the senior leadership level without direct authority.

* Excellent executive presentation skills and ability to travel regularly to bakery locations.

  
  

**Preferred**

* Direct restaurant or multi-unit operations leadership experience.

* Advanced experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, or comparable methodologies.

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, PMP, Prosci Change Management, or comparable certification.

* Experience within QSR, fast casual, retail, or another high-volume, multi-unit consumer environment.

* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree (MBA or related) preferred, or equivalent experience.

  

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

This position requires regular travel to bakery locations across multiple regions, including standing, walking, and observing operations on-site, as well as the ability to sit, use a computer, and participate in meetings for extended periods. These requirements may be met with or without reasonable accommodation.

existing_roles.title: General Manager, Data Operations
existing_roles.description:
**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About our Data Operations team**
----------------------------------

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale.

This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.

**About this role**
-------------------

As **General Manager of Data Operations** at David AI, you will lead one of the most critical functions at David AI. You’ll own a major slice of our Data Factory: the engine that powers high-quality, scalable data production. You’ll lead the team responsible for building and scaling pipelines, from 0 1 experiments that unlock new model capabilities to 1 N industrialization that processes data reliably and efficiently.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

* Build and lead a team of Data Product Operations Leads, to spin up and scale data pipelines, from early experiments to production systems that generate high-quality audio data at scale.
* Act as a thought partner to executive leadership on how we can evolve and scale delivery capabilities in service of customer needs.
* Continuously monitor and improve pipeline health, spotting issues in sourcing, quality, or process early and owning solutions end-to-end.
* Use metrics to drive decisions, tracking throughput, quality, and cost to guide prioritization and identify where to scale or invest next.
* Work with researchers at leading AI labs to identify new model capabilities and turn them into concrete data workflows and project plans.
* Partner with our internal research team to design and test new data shapes that unlock frontier model capabilities.
* Own outcomes across functions, designing systems, managing execution, unblocking bottlenecks, and ensuring delivery at both prototype and production scale.

**Your background looks like**
------------------------------

* 5 to 10+ years of experience in high-ownership roles (e.g., founder, GM, COO, or strategy/ops at a venture-backed startup).
* Prior experience scaling large-scale operational efforts at high-growth startups or fast-paced companies.
* Technical fluency with data and operations; SQL proficiency required.
* Prior experience designing and scaling systems, processes, and teams across different customer segments and product lines.
* A relentless operator with high standards, bias to action, and strong attention to detail.
* Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid pace; thrives in a “build while flying” environment.
* Low-ego, collaborative, and mission-driven, focused on team and company success.

**Bonus points if you have**
----------------------------

* Experience in data, ML, or large-scale operations.
* Background in CS, industrial engineering, or similar.

**Benefits**
------------

* Unlimited PTO.
* Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.
* FSA & HSA access.
* 401k access.
* Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.
* Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.

**Visas**
---------

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B *transfers*, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

Compensation Range: $205K - $235K

protected_roles.title: Quality Director
protected_roles.description:
**Summary**

Provides strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, ensuring that quality systems, processes, and practices support business objectives, customer requirements, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence. Establishes quality strategy, policies, objectives, and performance expectations and provides leadership across functions to drive continuous improvement, strengthen quality performance, mitigate risk, and support business growth.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, establishing priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with business and operational goals.
* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site's Quality Management System and associated quality policies, procedures, and controls.
* Serve as the site's senior quality leader and management representative for applicable ISO 9001, AS9100, and ISO 13485 quality management systems.
* Ensure continued compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, industry, and certification requirements, including applicable FDA, ITAR, ISO, and IPC requirements and standards.
* Provide leadership for quality planning related to processes, products, customers, and business requirements, with consideration for broader corporate quality objectives.
* Establish and monitor quality metrics and performance indicators. Identify trends, risks, and systemic issues and lead actions to improve quality performance.
* Provide quality performance, risk, and improvement recommendations to site and organizational leadership.
* Lead the Material Review Board (MRB) process and provide oversight for the disposition and control of nonconforming material and product.
* Provide leadership and oversight for corrective and preventive actions, root cause analysis, and systemic problem resolution in partnership with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and other functions.
* Lead quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, improving process capability, increasing throughput, and strengthening overall operational performance.
* Drive a culture of continuous improvement and quality ownership throughout the organization.
* Provide oversight of internal and external audit activities, certification requirements, customer audits, and resulting corrective actions.
* Partner with Supply Chain and suppliers to evaluate supplier quality performance, address quality risks, and ensure supplier quality systems meet business and customer requirements.
* Oversee the calibration system and applicable preventive maintenance controls to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
* Ensure appropriate training and organizational capability related to workmanship standards, acceptance criteria, quality systems, and regulatory/customer requirements.
* Support environmental management requirements, including applicable ISO 14001 responsibilities and site environmental management activities.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, and other functions to identify and mitigate quality and operational risks and improve customer outcomes.
* Provide quality leadership and expertise in support of new products, customers, programs, processes, and business opportunities.
* Promote awareness and understanding of regulatory, customer, and quality requirements throughout the organization.
* Lead, develop, and mentor Quality leaders and team members, building organizational capability and ensuring appropriate talent development and succession planning.
* Support corporate and site Lean/6S objectives and integrate quality principles into continuous improvement initiatives.
* Support and follow all applicable Quality Management System requirements related to quality, environmental, health, safety, and security.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**Job Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Advanced knowledge of quality management systems and quality principles within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, and other applicable regulatory and customer quality requirements.
* Working knowledge of FDA, ITAR, IPC, and applicable electronics manufacturing standards and requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to translate business objectives into quality strategies, priorities, metrics, and improvement initiatives.
* Strong knowledge of corrective action, root cause analysis, risk management, process improvement, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to analyze quality and operational data, identify trends and systemic risks, and develop effective corrective and preventive strategies.
* Strong business acumen with the ability to balance quality, customer, operational, financial, and business considerations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive results across functions without relying solely on direct authority.
* Strong leadership and organizational capability, including experience building, developing, and leading professional and technical teams.
* Ability to communicate effectively with customers, regulatory bodies, auditors, suppliers, and senior leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and applicable electronic manufacturing and quality systems.

**Experience/Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations, or a related technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible quality, engineering, or manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated experience leading a quality organization within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Experience managing multiple concurrent technical, quality, and operational priorities.
* Demonstrated experience influencing cross-functional leaders and driving organization-wide quality and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience interacting with customers, auditors, regulatory organizations, and senior business leadership.
* Demonstrated balance of strategic thinking, strong analytical capability, and effective execution.
* Strong business judgment, attention to detail, and written and verbal communication skills.

**Due to ITAR and / or CUI compliance, this position requires candidates to be a U.S. Citizen.**

Benefits Offered: Comprehensive benefit package including medical, dental and vision coverage; company-paid basic life/AD&D insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance; voluntary supplemental insurances, flexible spending accounts and employee assistance program (EAP). Sick Leave, Vacation Time, and company-paid Holidays are also provided as paid time off. NEOTech also provides a 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan option with a company match.

NEOTech is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

NEOTech has a long-standing commitment to maintaining a safe, quality-oriented and productive work environment. We also want all employees to perform their duties safely and efficiently, in a manner that protects their interests and those of their co-workers. We recognize that alcohol and drug abuse pose a threat to the health and safety of NEOTech employees and to the security of the Company’s equipment and facilities. For these reasons, NEOTech is committed to the elimination of drug and alcohol use and abuse in the workplace. Candidates being considered for hire must pass a pre-employment background check and drug test which include screening for illegal drugs and marijuana.

protected_roles.description:
About Us:

### ***Specialized Care for the Patients Who Need It Most.***

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals (NPH) is dedicated to providing unparalleled service to our patients, team members, physicians, and families. We dare to do things differently, bringing together compassionate care, specialized expertise, and an interdisciplinary approach to meet the unique needs of those we serve. It is this commitment that distinguishes NPH as the healthcare provider of choice.

As a national leader in behavioral healthcare, NPH specializes in caring for patients with acute psychiatric and complex medical needs. Our hospitals provide patient-centered care through an interdisciplinary, multi-specialty approach, ensuring our patients receive the specialized support they need when they need it most.

With locations in Indiana, Michigan, Texas, Ohio, and Arizona, we are expanding access to our unique model of care across the United States. Join NPH and become part of a team that is daring to do things differently and making a lasting difference in the lives of our patients, families, and communities every day.

Overview:

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals is looking for a Director of Quality and Risk at our **Huber Heights, OH** location. NPH is the national leader in providing medical and neurobehavioral care to patients in acute psychiatric distress. You will be joining a team of rock star staff who provide exceptional, patient-centered care and understand our patients are always our number one priority! The Director of Quality supports the implementation and monitoring of the quality assurance measurements and audits, and assists in improving patient safety processes throughout the hospital through coordinating and engaging in activities to proactively promote implementation of evidence based best practices and resolve deficiencies; plans, develops, and directs system activities and protocols across NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals; helps to prepare NPH facilities for surveys by accrediting and licensing agencies; serves as a resource to all departments and personnel.

**Benefits of joining NPH as a Director of Quality and Risk**

* Competitive pay rates
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* NPH 401(k) plan with up to 4% Company match
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Programs
* Generous PTO and Time Off Policy
* Special tuition offers through Capella University
* Work/life balance with great professional growth opportunities
* Employee Discounts through LifeMart

Responsibilities:

* Implements and monitors quality goals and objectives to measure the organization’s processes and outcomes while administering programs that focus on improved outcomes of patient care or patient safety.
* Interacts with physicians, nurses, department managers, supervisors, and any/all other staff members to provide resource information and identify new opportunities to improve service and reduce costs.
* Generates effectual quality related policies and procedures for the department and hospital that ensures compliance with JC, OSHA, CDC, CMS and other county, state, and federal regulatory agencies.
* Prepares reports, presentations and statistical data that go to the Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement Committee Meetings, facility's administration and other committees as needed. Analyzes data to identify trends and resource utilization for use in optimizing compliance.
* Assists with the annual assessment of the quality control programs from the prior year activities.
* Investigates incidents within the facility and coordinates with the Corporate Quality team to complete the root cause analysis and develop action plans to prevent incidents in the future.
* Establish a structure to ensure that patient care activities are addressed in a coordinated manner involving quality improvement.
* Prepares the agenda for the Quality Council Committee meetings and holds regularly scheduled meetings.
* Provides educational offerings for orientation and on-going in-services.
* Performs mortality reviews in conjunction with the mortality committee and holds regularly scheduled mortality committee meetings.
* Ensures all staff receive proper education on new or revised state and/ or federal regulations or Joint Commission standards.
* Participates in Multi-disciplinary patient centered case conferences, as appropriate.
* Assess and evaluate patients with infections and monitor patient outcomes on an ongoing basis.
* Initiates follow-up on employee/patient exposures to communicable diseases.
* Participates in root-cause analysis, sentinel events, adverse events and identifies trends as directed by regulation. Recommends ways to redesign systems for improvements if needed.
* Oversee Patient Advocacy program.
* Establishes/maintains good relationships with COO, CEO and DON’s and department leaders to promote a cooperative and constructive environment for improvement.
* Promote “Quality is everyone’s business” to gain support, understanding and ownership among staff.
* Other duties as may be assigned.
* Complies with hospital expectations regarding ethical behavior and standards of conduct.
* Complies with federal and hospital requirements in the areas of protected health information & patient privacy.
* Understands and adheres to NPH’s compliance standards as they appear in NPH’s Corporate Compliance Policy, Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest Policy.
* Keeps abreast of all pertinent federal, state and hospital regulations, laws and policies as they presently exist and as they change or are modified.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

* Bachelor's Degree in healthcare field or pertinent program required. Master's Degree preferred.
* 3+ years of relevant healthcare quality and risk management experience. Prior leadership experience preferred.
* Excellent verbal communication skills necessary in order present quality reports.
* Maintain effective contacts with a variety of Hospital Personnel.
* Professional knowledge of clinical practice, leadership, performance improvement and research statistics in order to conduct surveillance and prepare related reports at a level normally acquired through the completion of a Bachelor’s degree in related field.

Founded in 1982 as Joliet Area Community Hospice, Lightways Hospice and Serious Illness Care is an independent, nonprofit healthcare provider licensed in 11 counties in northwest Illinois. We provide exceptional serious illness care, hospice care and grief support for adults and children.

The majority of our direct patient care is in the field with Lightways team members providing care in the home, nursing facility or assisted living facility. We also have a 24-bed inpatient unit in Joliet. Non-clinical staff are based out of our Joliet administrative offices.

**Director of Quality and Compliance**

The Director of Quality & Compliance provides administrative oversight for Quality, Compliance, Medical Records, and Risk Management functions, while also serving as the organization’s designated Compliance Officer.

This role delivers strategic and operational leadership for the Lightways Quality Assessment & Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, regulatory compliance, accreditation readiness, clinical education, and risk management. The Director is responsible for developing, implementing, and evaluating robust systems that promote safety, regulatory adherence, and high-quality care across all organizational operations.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Reference, research, report, track, and monitor compliance and quality-related data.
* Develop, implement, and evaluate strategies for quality assurance, performance improvement, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
* Create and maintain the organization’s annual Quality and Compliance Plans and Reports.
* Lead quarterly Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) meetings.
* Review Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) survey data, complaints, and incident reports to inform improvement strategies.
* Develop and deliver education, policies, and process improvements to promote accurate, timely, and compliant clinical documentation across the organization.

  

**Education/Experience:**

* Master's degree in healthcare or related field (required)
* Management experience with hospice and/or palliative care experience preferred.
* Certification in a specialist area preferred; (e.g. Hospice and Palliative Nursing (CHPN), Pediatrics or Geriatrics)

  

**Benefits:**

* 401(k) matching
* Health Insurance
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Personal Time Off
* Holiday Paid

protected_roles.description:
This position is incentive eligible.  
  
  

Do you have the career opportunities as a Group Quality Director you want with your current employer? We have an exciting opportunity for you to join HCA Laboratory Services which is part of the nation's leading provider of healthcare services, HCA Healthcare.

Travel is Required. You will Support 5- Divisions. Must Reside in Utah, Idaho, Nevada, North Carolina, Virginia, Alaska or in the Nashville, TN area.

Job Summary and Qualifications

The Group Quality Director is responsible for implementation of the Laboratory Service Line quality and performance improvement programs for our National Group. This position applies quality and performance improvement approaches to identify and quantify improvement opportunities, facilitate and organization process improvement efforts, drive improvement, and measure outcomes. This role supervises Quality Coordinators in assigned divisions. You will be responsible for laboratory regulatory agency accreditation preparedness, tracking and reporting of specific information; auditing and analysis of processes and systems; statistical analysis of data; formulation of recommendations; and creation of written and verbal reports. The position also requires skills for developing and presenting related training programs for laboratory colleagues and for preparing presentations to and for management.

In This Role You Will:

* Deploy the laboratory clinical quality infrastructure across the National Group divisions.
* Partner with leaders to identify and coordinate implementation of continual improvement projects to improve quality performance.
* Facilitate the growth of vision of laboratory quality and performance, including the dissemination of "best practices" across the country.
* Lead regional process improvement initiatives, provide feedback on standardization opportunities and evaluate success through pre-established criteria.
* Assist with appropriate and timely response to Serious Patient Adverse Events (SPAE)s that involve laboratory operations.
* Lead proactive laboratory quality and safety activities to create hospital laboratories that are highly reliable as reflected in reduced errors, elimination of unsafe processes and increase involvement of staff and pathology medical directors toward a culture of safety.
* Contribute to the achievement of laboratory business and financial goals through optimal division and group performance in quality and patient safety.
* Interface with appropriate personnel at HCA to leverage corporate resources, programs, tools and methodologies for benefit of hospital laboratories.
* Collaborate with and support hospital quality, risk, safety and infection prevention leaders to achieve top ranking in national and state publicly reported data initiatives.
* Participate in regular analysis of laboratory quality and risk performance data, and plan steps for ongoing improvement.
* Work with Corporate and Division medical leaders to support data analysis, reporting, process and outcomes improvement.
* Contribute to ongoing enhancement of enterprise quality reporting methods and dashboards.
* Continuously monitor and evaluate quality outcomes across the group and division, while noting trends and identifying and prioritizing opportunities to improve.
* Assist divisions in building a proactive quality department by implementing processes to support accreditation and regulatory inspections.
* Facilitate and/or lead process improvement teams as needed to achieve quality improvement goals.
* Serve as a regulatory resource regarding state and federal regulations and standards, including but not limited to CMS, CLIA, CAP, and TJC.
* Demonstrate personal responsibility for professional development, and promoting and supporting laboratory quality leaders and division data analysts.
* Promote a culture that is positive, values individual strengths, takes risks and is committed to optimal patient care and compliance with standards.
* Attend HCA-mandated training and meeting all ethics and compliance standards and requirements.
* Develop and implement projects as directed by AVP, Quality and CLO.

What Qualifications You Will Need:

* Bachelor's degree in a clinical laboratory, chemical, biological science or related field is required.
* Master's degree in a related field is preferred.
* 3+ years of experience in quality improvement is required.
* 1+ years of experience in clinical laboratory is preferred.
* Management experience is preferred.
* Previous experience within a multi-facility environment is preferred.
* Clinical licensure, Laboratory Medical Technology or RN is preferred.
* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) is preferred.

##### **Benefits**

Work from Home, offers a total rewards package that supports the health, life, career and retirement of our colleagues. The available plans and programs include:

* **Comprehensive benefits** for medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, behavioral health and telemedicine services
* **Wellbeing support,** including free counseling and referral services
* **Time away from work** programs for paid time off, paid family leave, long- and short-term disability coverage and leaves of absence
* **Savings and retirement resources**, including a 401(k) Plan with a 100% match on 3% to 9% of pay (based on years of service), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, flexible spending accounts, preferred banking partnerships, retirement readiness tools, rollover support and financial wellbeing counseling
* **Education support** through tuition assistance, student loan assistance, certification support, dependent scholarships and a partnership with Galen College of Nursing
* **Additional benefits** for fertility and family building, adoption assistance, life insurance, supplemental health protection plans, auto and home insurance, legal counseling, identity theft protection and consumer discounts

Learn more about Employee Benefits

***Note: Eligibility for benefits may vary by location.***

**Integrated Regional Labs** is a full service providerfor clinical laboratory and anatomic pathology services, providing hospitals, physicians, and clients with**timely diagnostic information** for patient care. Our infrastructure includes a fullyautomated esoteric core laboratory in Fort Lauderdale, a histology and microbiology operation in Largo,Florida, and a network of hospital based **rapid-response** laboratories present in fourHCA Healthcare divisions within the state of Florida. Our core laboratories support **more than250** acute and rehab hospitals, physician practices, surgery centers and commercialaccounts.

HCA Healthcare has been recognized as one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies® by the Ethisphere Institute more than ten times. In recent years, HCA Healthcare spent an estimated $3.7 billion in cost for thedelivery of charitable care, uninsured discounts, and other uncompensated expenses.

HCA Healthcare Co-Founder

Be a part of an organization that invests in you! We are reviewing applications for our Group Quality Director - Lab Service Line opening. Qualified candidates will be contacted for interviews. Submit your application and ***help us raise the bar in patient care!***

Lead a High-Performing Manufacturing Operation and Drive Operational Excellence

* Safety performance and employee engagement
* Product quality and customer satisfaction
* On-time delivery and schedule attainment
* Cost control and operational efficiency
* Maintenance and facility reliability
* Continuous improvement and Lean manufacturing initiatives

Key Responsibilities
  

* Lead daily plant operations to ensure safety, quality, delivery, and cost targets are achieved.

* Foster a culture built on accountability, trust, teamwork, and servant leadership.

* Conduct regular Gemba walks, safety reviews, audits, and performance discussions.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, and company safety standards.

What We're Looking For
  
Required Qualifications
  

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or a related field, or equivalent manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years of experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or comparable site leader.
* Proven success leading salaried supervisors and managers in a multi-shift manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost metrics.
* Experience working with ERP/MRP systems for production scheduling, inventory, and shop floor operations.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing labor, maintenance, and capital budgets.
* Knowledge of production scheduling, capacity planning, and manufacturing operations.
* Working knowledge of OSHA and environmental compliance requirements.
* Excellent communication and team leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications
  

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Experience leading operational turnarounds or transformational change initiatives.
* Background in manufacturing environments involving assembly, metal fabrication, sheet metal, packaging, mechanical components, fasteners, or related industrial products.
* Experience driving cultural transformation and employee engagement initiatives.

**The successful candidate will be:**  

* A servant leader who develops people and builds strong teams.
* A culture builder capable of leading organizational change.
* A proactive problem solver who challenges convention and drives improvement.
* A leader who creates accountability rather than simply managing tasks.
* Equally comfortable on the production floor and in strategic planning discussions.
* Focused on measurable results while maintaining a people-first approach.

* Opportunity to lead a highly visible manufacturing operation.
* Strong support from executive leadership.
* Collaborative, team-oriented culture.
* Ability to drive operational improvements and leave a lasting impact.
* Opportunity to develop employees, strengthen culture, and improve business performance.

Apply today and become the leader who drives the next chapter of operational excellence.

* Competitive medical, dental, vision, and prescription insurance coverage
* 401k with a company match

**Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all day-to-day manufacturing operations at the site, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production. This role owns execution of production, cost, delivery, and safety performance, while aligning with corporate standards across quality, engineering, supply chain, and HR. The Plant Manager drives operational discipline, team performance, and continuous improvement to deliver consistent, predictable results.

  

**Company Overview:**

PTA Plastics, an employee-owned and innovative leader in the plastic injection molding, contract manufacturing and tool-building industry, is looking for a Plant Manager to join our dynamic team.

At PTA Plastics, we’re more than just a manufacturer; we partner with Fortune 500 OEMs in the medical device, defense, homeland security, and technology sectors, constantly pushing the boundaries of product development and manufacturing excellence. As an employee-owned company, every team member has a stake in our success, creating a collaborative and entrepreneurial environment where innovation thrives.

**Pay:** $150,000 - $190,000 annually

  

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Site P&L Performance**

* Own site-level financial performance

* Deliver budgeted profitability, labor efficiency, and cost targets

* Control overtime, scrap, and operating expenses

  

**Production & Operational Execution**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations

* Ensure schedule attainment and on-time delivery

* Drive production efficiency, uptime, and throughput

* Remove operational roadblocks quickly

* Lead and resolve customer escalations at the plant level

  

**Safety & Compliance**

* Own plant safety performance

* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company standards

* Drive a proactive, behavior-based safety culture

  

**People Leadership & Culture**

* Lead and develop plant leadership team and floor personnel

* Drive accountability, performance management, and clear expectations

* Build a high-performance, no-excuses culture

  

**Execution of Corporate Quality Standards**

* Ensure adherence to corporate Quality Management System (QMS)

* Support and enforce corrective actions

* Hold production teams accountable for quality at the source

  

**Execution of Corporate Engineering Standards**

* Maintain schedule discipline and production alignment with planning

* Resolve plant-level material and supply issues

* Support inventory control and flow

  

**Cross Functional Alignment**

* Corporate Quality

* Corporate Engineering

* Corporate Supply Chain

* Corporate HR

  

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives

* Reduce scrap, downtime, and inefficiencies

* Improve labor utilization and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)

  

**Qualifications & Requirements:**

#### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field required (or equivalent combination of education and experience)
* 7–10+ years of manufacturing experience, preferably in injection molding or a similar high-volume, process-driven environment
* 3–5+ years of leadership experience managing production teams and plant operations
* Proven track record of delivering results in:
  + Production output and schedule attainment
  + Cost control and labor efficiency
  + Safety and quality performance
* Experience leading in a metrics-driven environment (OEE, scrap, uptime, etc.)
* Hands-on experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction initiatives
* Experience working within structured corporate environments with cross-functional support (Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, HR)
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and production planning processes

#### **Technical & Industry Knowledge**

* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including production processes, workflow optimization, and plant performance metrics (OEE, uptime, scrap, labor efficiency)

* Working knowledge of injection molding processes, materials, tooling, and secondary operations (or similar high-volume manufacturing processes)

* Understanding of maintenance and reliability principles, including preventive maintenance and equipment uptime optimization

* Experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction methodologies (5S, Kaizen, standard work, etc.)

* Knowledge of quality systems and practices, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and adherence to QMS standards (ISO or similar)

* Familiarity with production scheduling, capacity planning, and inventory flow within an ERP/MRP environment

* Understanding of workplace safety standards and regulatory compliance (OSHA, environmental requirements)

* Ability to interpret and act on operational data to drive performance improvements

  

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move around the production floor for extended periods.
* Capable of lifting and carrying heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination for handling small tools, machine components, and molds.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities.
* Comfortable wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses, gloves, and ear protection.
* Occasional bending, kneeling, and reaching to access equipment and perform maintenance tasks.
* Good vision and color perception for inspecting parts and identifying any defects or abnormalities.
* Ability to work in temperature-controlled environments and withstand exposure to noise levels associated with manufacturing machinery.
* Ability to receive, comprehend and utilize required training from OSHA and Company including but not limited to the following:
* Hazard Communication
* Lock Out/Tag Out

  

**ITAR Requirements:** To conform to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3), applicants for employment at PTA Plastics must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawfully admitted for permanent residence into the U.S. (i.e., current green card holder), or lawfully admitted as a refugee or granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1157-1158.

Reporting to a Director of Clinical Quality Assurance, the Sr. Manager of Clinical Quality Assurance serves as a Development QA (DevQA) representative on the development team assuring quality and regulatory compliance related to GCPs and other related activities performed by Clinical Study (Trial) Teams. You will provide support and promote collaboration internally and externally to ensure all systems, processes and their outcomes comply with applicable international and national standards, regulations, and guidelines.

**What You'll Do:**

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to Serve and maintain qualification as a GCP Subject Matter Expert (SME) as well as contribute to and support the maintenance of a risk-based and scientific-based quality system to support GCP. You’ll also:

  

* Ensure that a strategic audit plan is implemented and activities are conducted and reported according to SOPs and regulations.
* Perform audits of investigator sites, TMFs, vendors, and internal systems/processes.
* Support the evaluation and acceptability of clinical vendors/suppliers.
* Support strategic direction with cross functional working groups to identify and mitigate GCP quality and compliance issues.
* Establish and foster compliance with ICH E6 Guideline for Good Clinical Practice.
* Provide support and coaching to other staff members to develop additional quality and auditing resources.
* Manage quality documentation in Veeva QMS.
* Act as company’s representative during regulatory agency inspections.

**Who You Are:**

Basic Qualifications

You meet the following minimum education and experience requirements:

* BA/BS degree in Biology or Chemistry or related life sciences discipline along with a minimum of 5 years of GCP experience.
  

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to meeting the basic qualifications above, you will also possess some or all of the following:

* An understanding and practical working knowledge of clinical regulations, good clinical practices, development processes, and regulatory inspection procedures.
* Experience in developing SOPs, reviewing internal clinical, regulatory, and medical processes to ensure they are consistent with current regulatory and GCP requirements.
* GCP audit experience with the ability to conduct external audits of investigator sites, CROs, supporting laboratories, and monitoring organizations with responsibility for writing audit reports and reviewing and tracking CAPAs.
* Ability to conduct external audits of investigator sites, CROs, supporting laboratories, and monitoring organizations with responsibility for writing audit reports and reviewing and tracking CAPAs.
* Experience in supporting regulatory agency inspections and working with regulators and internal staff to help prepare for inspections.
* Broad knowledge of risk-based quality systems and approaches consistent with ICH E6 for Good Clinical Practice.
* Solid experience with Phases I-IV (particularly Phase III); experience with Regulatory approval, NDAs and MAAs is preferred.
* Ability to foster a collaborative/partnership environment, adapt to other personalities in a respectful manner that is conducive to goal achievement and team. building while maintaining quality and compliance.
* Highly organized with a strong attention to detail, clarity, accuracy, and conciseness.
  

**Where You’ll Work**

This is a fully remote role. It can be performed effectively from anywhere while staying connected to your Insmed team and community. Occasional travel for team meetings or events may be expected.

**Travel Requirements**

This position involves frequent domestic/international travel (up to 25-30%) to support clinical QA including external audits.
